title: Python attribute-write #17 (N7): cross-module __class__ write leaves an outside receiver resolving — scoped before building (DEC-303 a88)
description: HELD RECORD, split out of GCLI-156 by DEC-303 (a88) arm A (ODOC-640, recorded 2026-11-27T11:54Z): #17 (N7) moves to its own held task AFTER GCLI-156 rounds, and is scoped before any build. Shape: an __init__ that writes self.__class__ = Other leaves an outside receiver x = C(); x.m() resolving across a module boundary. Dev measured 2026-11-27 at origin/dev 1ea3432 gives the wrong edge m.py:C.m. Origin: GCLI-151 split under (a80) item 6; described in GCLI-156 before the (a88) split. SCOPING CONDITION (a88 item 2, verbatim): if it does not fit two rounds, an A/B comes to opum-doc on whether it stays a hold item or becomes a documented limitation (0 occurrences on the pins). So the first step is not a build: scope the cross-module propagation, write the two-round plan with its fixtures, and if it cannot fit two rounds bring the bounded A/B to the leader instead of building. MEASUREMENT on which arm A was chosen (a81 item 3, read-only, Python ast, five pins at flask 49943b5a, httpx 7cff5f79, jinja 5ef70112, rich 3a109ccd, tqdm 9cf5a12b): 483 files, 841 classes, 1450 self-receiver calls, 992 instance writes, a synthetic positive control the same script detected, and ZERO self.__class__ assignments on all five pins (per pin flask/httpx/jinja/rich/tqdm 0/0). No DEC-182 path class; expected files src/python/calls.ts and test/python-hops.test.ts.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The shape is scoped before it is built: the task records the two-round plan with its fixtures and the occurrence measurement it was scoped against, or brings a bounded A/B to opum-doc if it cannot fit two rounds
A red-before green-after fixture for the outside receiver across a module boundary, with a resolving twin and a mutant per path observed red

Removal-only holds: the flag-extended subset check over the five pins, every fixture and the corpus shows no created and no flag-changed in-repo edge, group count stated with a floor equal to the exact count, an observed-red control and every removed edge named in the PR
No DEC-182 path class is touched and no dependency is added

plan: 1. Re-measure the dev wrong edge on the current dev (done in this scope): the cross-module x = C(); x.m() after self.__class__ = Other in __init__ still resolves m.py:C.m; same-module too; the twin without the write resolves as expected.

2. Build one guard, instance-dispatch only: thread an instanceReceiver flag through methodLookup from the call sites that resolve an INSTANCE to a class (the 6d/R4 constructed-local, module-constructed and imported-instance paths, E1 constructed receivers, alias receivers), and refuse when classAttributeWritten(receiver MRO, __class__) is true. Class-level calls (C.m(C())) and super() stay resolving; the probe shows the naive MRO-wide guard would also refuse C.m(C()), so the flag is the design point.

3. Fixtures per (a83) item 2: the written attribute across a module boundary, a NEIGHBOUR attribute on the same instance, the receiver itself (the C() construction edge), before and after the write, same-module, dotted constructor m.C().m(), imported instance, a descendant D(C), the twin without the write, an unrelated class twin, and the class-level C.m(C()) twin that must NOT refuse.

4. Mutants, each observed red on a predicted subset: guard off; guard applied to class-level calls (class-level twin red); classLevelWrites instead of classAttrWrites (instance-write fixtures red); receiver-MRO-only instead of ancestors (descendant fixture red).

5. Proof floor: kit fixtures added, floor equal to the exact group count; the scope probe measured 0 pin removals on dev c70c624 over 1526 groups, so expect only fixture removals; both controls and the notes comparator firing.
implementationNotes: SCOPING DONE 2026-11-27 on dev c70c624 (DEC-303 (a88) item 2; leader brief: scope first, no build, do not change the hold label). RE-MEASUREMENT: the wrong edge is still there on current dev. m.py class Other with m(), class C with __init__ setting self.__class__ = Other and its own m(); app.py from m import C; x = C(); x.m() gives app.py:3:1 -> m.py:C.m (resolved in-repo). The same-module form gives m.py:11:1 -> C.m. The twin with the __init__ write removed resolves to C.m as expected, so the write is what should stop it and does not. PROBE OF THE INTENDED GUARD (disposable copy of dev, guard at methodLookup: refuse when classAttributeWritten(MRO, "__class__") on non-super calls): the cross-module, same-module, neighbour x.n(), dotted constructor m.C().m() and descendant shapes all refuse; an unrelated class is untouched; a class-level C.m(C()) ALSO refuses, which the shape does not call for and which a reviewer would flag (the runtime class of an instance does not change which function C.m names). Blast radius on the pins: 0 removed edges and 0 bin changes over all 1526 groups at dev c70c624 (consistent with the (a81) item 3 measurement of ZERO self.__class__ assignments on the five pins), so the build removes nothing on the pins and everything it removes is fixture-driven. FIT: TWO ROUNDS — one guard with an instanceReceiver flag threaded from the instance-resolving call sites (the class-level calls stay resolving), ~12 fixtures, 4 mutants and the standard proof; no core resolution-model change, no dependency. The fallback if round 2 blocks on something the fix introduces follows (a89): drop the fix commit and carry the shape to opum-doc rather than force a third round.
